highlights.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
highlights.description: The iPhone maker appears to be building agents that can compete with the likes of Meta Muse, Instinct, Claude, and OpenAI Dots.

highlights.title: Anthropic’s IPO Triumph
highlights.description: Anthropic pulled it off. The biggest pure-play AI company out there, maker of the Claude line of AI models, went public on Thursday, with its shares jumping as much as 39% above its IPO price. The stock settled back a bit to close at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price. That gave it a market capitalization of $1.76 trillion, assuming you include all options, restricted stock units and convertible notes that might one day become shares. highlights.title: Asian Chip Stocks Slide as Anthropic IPO Fails to Dispel AI Woes
highlights.description: Asia’s chip-related shares resumed their selloff on Friday despite Anthropic PBC’s blockbuster listing, a sign that concerns about the artificial intelligence trade, which have been building for months, continue to dominate investor sentiment.

highlights.title: Anthropic Shares Drop Post-Market on Apple’s AI Agent Plans
highlights.description: Shares of Anthropic PBC fell more than 3% in after-hours trading following their New York debut, as Apple Inc. plans to develop an autonomous AI agent and investor caution over the AI trade weighed on momentum throughout the day.
